To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) a new 3D finite element model of the human tibia was developed, (2) the model accurately predicted the mechanical properties of the bone and the experimental results, and (3) the model can be used as a reliable tool for investigating the mechanical behavior of the tibia in various loading conditions.
the mechanical properties and microstructure of the tibia can be determined by the combination of a CT scan and the finite element method.
the 3D printed tibia model was validated and can be used for future research.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the validation of a 3D FE model of the tibia based on CT scans and the mechanical characterization of a new material, a polyurethane foam, which is a substitute for the spongy bone.
the development of a new method for the mechanical validation of a 3D model of the tibia.
the validation of finite element models of the human lower leg and foot using experimental measurements.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the current study provides an accurate and detailed model of human tibia.
the finite element model of the tibia is validated.
the current model is a good model to predict the mechanical properties of the tibia and can be used for further biomechanical studies.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we developed a 3D model of tibia based on CT scan images and validated the model using the experimental data of human cadaveric specimen.
the mechanical properties of human bones are highly dependent on their anatomical locations and that the mechanical properties are not uniform within the bone.
the FE model of tibia based on CT scan images is a reliable model for predicting mechanical behavior of the human tibia.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the tibia is a highly heterogeneous structure with different mechanical properties.
the mechanical properties of the tibia and fibula are similar, and that the tibia and the fibula should be modeled as one unit.
we have shown that the use of a 3D-printed tibia model for the purpose of mechanical testing is feasible, and can be used for the purpose of studying the biomechanics of the tibia.
